# Devpost draft (generated by `ml/evaluation/build_writeup.py`)

## What is simulated and what is real (honesty statement)

**Simulated in the sandbox:** the company (150 employees), its asset register, SaaS subscriptions, seat-usage logs and 90-day purchase history, and the vendors (two vendor agents we wrote, each with its own PayPal sandbox merchant account).
**Real:** benchmark prices come from the real Channel3 catalog (five anchor products). Mandates, verification, orders, subscriptions, the ledger and the dashboard are real code against real PayPal sandbox APIs. [CONFIRM WITH BAI/SWE before keeping this sentence: executePurchase must create and capture real sandbox orders, not just generate a reference.]
**AI components:** an LLM (`deepseek-chat`) compiles plain-English policies; the planning agent is deterministic, and a deterministic verifier decides whether money moves. [CONFIRM: model name actually deployed.]
**Measured on synthetic data:** every ML and backtest number below. They are upper bounds, not field results. The policy and abuse test suites were written by the team and are published in the repo.

## Policy compiler

On a held-out set of 32 hand-written policies (run once, prompt frozen), the compiler produced the exactly correct policy for 100.0% of 18 clear inputs and guessed on 0.0% of 14 ambiguous or adversarial inputs (it asks a question instead). Schema validity 100.0%.

## Break-it Arena

45 of the 45 attacks we could drive at the deterministic verifier were stopped safely, with false-block rate 0/3 on legitimate purchases. 21 further cases are not yet runnable and are not counted. Our first run found fail-open gaps in the verifier; they were fixed (see `arena/findings/FINDINGS.md`).

## Benchmark coverage

Of 30 business-hardware queries against Channel3, 14 returned a usable benchmark (at least 3 priced, in-stock offers). Docking stations were reliable; laptops were the weakest category, so the demo anchors on five specific products.

## Savings projection and ML (synthetic)

Replaying 90 days of synthetic purchasing under the demo policy: 16 auto-approved, 14 escalated for human approval, 5 blocked by the circuit breaker. Realized savings (auto-approved only) $1,540.21, of which $1,480.03 comes from choosing the cheaper vendor and the rest from negotiation. The top three purchases account for 48.3% of positive savings.

Full tables: `docs/evaluation.md`. Limitations: the generator makes cleanly separable behaviour, planted anomalies are 30% of the history, and savings depend on our simulated vendors.
